Table: Coverage of nominal 90% intervals for fruit from consignments that supplied no standards, by how the standards were spread over consignments (mean over the setting-pipeline combinations, 300 repetitions each; in parentheses: combinations flagged as too narrow / combinations). The instrument settings alone have the 20 × 1 design. TJ+B: leave-one-consignment-out (hierarchical) jackknife+; Split: half the standards for transfer, half for calibration; LGO-CV+N: CV+ with consignments as folds but fruit as units; Gauss-LGO and ANOVA-PI: Gaussian and random-effects intervals from leave-one-consignment-out errors. The first four methods treat samples as the unit, the last four consignments.

Table: Harvest-maturity screening of mango at 14% dry matter with 90% intervals, slope/bias correction, for fruit from consignments that supplied no standards. Immature passed: percentage of truly immature fruit (DM < 14%) declared mature, mean (range) over the season shift and the three handheld-instrument pairs; referred: percentage of all fruit whose interval contains 14%. Designs: consignments × fruit per consignment (20 × 1: instrument pairs only). 200 repetitions. PDS results: Supplementary Table S14.
r_abstract_app: In a mango harvest-maturity check at 14% dry matter, passing fruit on the predicted value alone accepted 36–41% of immature fruit; 90% intervals cut this to 3.2% with reference fruit from ten consignments and 9.8% with fruit from two.
r_cover_app: In a harvest-maturity check of mango at the recommended minimum of 14% dry matter, deciding on the predicted value alone passed 36–41% of immature fruit; intervals from well-spread reference fruit reduced this to 3.2%, against 9.8% with fruit from two consignments, and flagged the fruit that needed a second measurement.
r_conclusion_app: In a harvest-maturity check of mango, intervals from well-spread reference fruit reduced the share of immature fruit passed as mature from 36% (predicted value alone) to 3.2%, at the cost of referring about half of the fruit for a second measurement.
